public_rationale: The records do not establish the universal claim. Gamma is a serious counterexample candidate: Stripe documents subscriptions, and its CEO reports profitability. limitations: The quarter and meaning of economic viability require interpretation.
The Gamma interview is contributed content, not an independently verified financial report.
This outcome does not imply that subscriptions are economically impossible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The monthly subscription model does not make economic sense for any LLM-connected service.

statement.excerpt: Both assumptions were wrong, because the monthly subscription model does not make sense for any service connected to a Large Language Model.

from_speaker: for any service connected to a Large Language Model
our_interpretation: The ordinary economic reading is that no LLM-connected service can sustain monthly subscription pricing under actual customer usage.
A subscription may include disclosed usage limits. Monthly billing alone does not qualify if customers also pay their actual token consumption.
I use January–March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before the post, for this ongoing observation.

A counterexample must connect subscription revenue to the recurring costs of delivering that service. Company-wide profitability without the relevant pricing and cost breakdown is suggestive but insufficient.
No particular company's monetary metric is asserted, so metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Representative service-level financial evidence establishes that monthly subscriptions cannot cover recurring delivery costs under actual usage, with evidence sufficient to justify the universal scope.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one LLM-connected service demonstrates sustainable positive unit economics from monthly subscriptions during the target period without billing each user's actual token consumption.
